# Consumer -> Lakebase write path, as deployed on 2026-11-20 (read-only inspection, captured 2026-11-21 07:20-07:45 UTC)

## Consumer (exported job notebook manufacturing_realtime_consumer_<ts>, generated by client/src/lib/notebook-template.ts)
Kafka (MSK, topic pharma-twin.manufacturing.realtime, 3 partitions, startingOffsets latest)
  -> Spark Real-Time Mode, .trigger(realTime="5 minutes"), .outputMode("update").foreach(RealtimeDualWriter())
  -> LakebaseWriter (one per Kafka partition/task): psycopg2, ONE connection per open() (per 5-min epoch),
     execute_values(page_size 100) + COMMIT when 100 rows are buffered or 100 ms passed, synchronous inside
     process() (the task waits for the flush), autocommit off, synchronous_commit on (server default)
  -> AppSseWriter: best-effort background POST to /api/sss/ingest (non-blocking queue, never back-pressures)
Job cluster: DBR 18.2, m5d.xlarge (4 vCPU), STANDARD engine (no Photon), fixed workers (2 on 11-20; app sizing gives 1).
The consumer is NOT row-by-row and does not reconnect per batch; the per-row cost sits in Postgres (below).

## Producer (exported job notebook manufacturing_realtime_producer_<ts>)
TARGET_RECORDS_PER_SEC = 500 (setup mode_configs.realtime.rate_hz = 500); kafka-python, acks=1, linger_ms=0,
key = sensor_name  (=> every sensor is pinned to one Kafka partition, see 03_partition_skew.txt)

## Pipeline branch primary endpoint
autoscaling 0.5-4 CU, scale-to-zero suspend 24 h, PostgreSQL 17.12, shared_buffers 230 MB (at capture),
max_wal_size 1 GB, synchronous_commit on, logical_decoding_work_mem 64 MB, max_connections 901.

## Triggers on public.sensor_readings (parent; the FOR EACH ROW ones are cloned onto all 240 partitions)
trg_lakets_lvc                       AFTER INSERT                      FOR EACH ROW        lakets._lvc_trigger_fn()
trg_lakets_sync                      AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE  FOR EACH ROW        lakets._sync_trigger_fn()
trg_lakets_rollup_invalidation       AFTER UPDATE OR DELETE            FOR EACH ROW        lakets._rollup_invalidation_trigger_fn()
trg_lakets_rollup_bulk_invalidation  AFTER INSERT  (transition table)  FOR EACH STATEMENT  lakets._bulk_import_invalidation()
trg_lakets_touch_chunk               AFTER INSERT                      FOR EACH STATEMENT  (on 98 partitions)
Per INSERTED ROW this runs two PL/pgSQL functions, each doing: lakets._resolve_partition_parent() (pg_inherits
lookup), a registry SELECT, format() + dynamic EXECUTE of one INSERT (shadow) or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
(last-value cache, 23 rows, 18.8 M updates so far, 95 % HOT).

## Tables (pg_total_relation_size)
lakets_cdf._shadow_manufacturing_sensor_readings  6,620 MB, ~28.0 M rows, unpartitioned, REPLICA IDENTITY FULL,
                                                  unique index on id; only ever INSERTed (no retention)
public.sensor_readings                            240 partitions of 15 min, 7.16 GB total (~107 MB / 430 k rows each),
                                                  1 index (event_time DESC); registry retention_interval NULL,
                                                  tiering disabled
public._lvc_sensor_readings                       23 rows, 1.9 MB
Indexes: none missing or redundant on the hot path (1 btree on the ChronoTable, 1 unique on the shadow).

## WAL per inserted row
LakeTS 0.1.0 row triggers: 820 B (server-side bench on a branch of this database, 04) - identical to the live
primary's ratio. Every row is written three times (chronotable + its index, shadow + its index, LVC update).
